core_obligations: Choose a K-injective complex I^bullet with injective terms representing K, and recall that I^bullet|_U is again K-injective, so all three derived functors in the triangle are obtained by applying the underlying functors to I^bullet (proof lines 8638-8644).
Reduce to the abelian level: it suffices to prove that for an injective O_X-module I the sequence 0 -> Gamma_Z(X, I) -> Gamma(X, I) -> Gamma(U, I) -> 0 is short exact (proof lines 8645-8651).
Conclude the exactness from the cited surjectivity result on restrictions and the definitions (proof lines 8652-8653).
proof_roadmap: Use a K-injective representative with injective terms.
Note the restriction to the open complement stays K-injective.
Reduce to the short exact sequence for an injective module and invoke the cited surjectivity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the functorial distinguished triangle RGamma_Z(X, K) -> RGamma(X, K) -> RGamma(U, K) -> RGamma_Z(X, K)[1] in D(O_X(X)) for i : Z -> X closed with open complement U. The proof represents K by a K-injective complex with injective terms, uses that its restriction to U is again K-injective so that each derived functor in the triangle is computed by applying the corresponding underlying functor, and thereby reduces the triangle to the short exact sequence 0 -> Gamma_Z(X, I) -> Gamma(X, I) -> Gamma(U, I) -> 0 for an injective module I (proof lines 8638-8652). H2: the passage from the derived statement to a single short exact sequence of injective modules is the substance.
